rows.title: Continued Investigation of Path Dependence and Value Divergence

rows.summary: Interpretation of experiment 78 indicates that interaction-coupling between agents acts to canalize state-space trajectories, constraining variance. To address identified uncertainty regarding coupling strength, a new experimental hypothesis is proposed to systematically vary coupling coefficients.
rows.title: Interpreting Canalization in Agent Value Convergence

rows.summary: Reviewed experiment exp-divergent-values-test-78, which showed that interaction-coupling constrains variance (divergence ratio 1.028, within tolerance 1.1). Interpretation suggests that canalization effectively limits value divergence in the tested system. Proceeding with refinement of the hypothesis to explore the limits of this stabilization under higher coupling variance.
rows.title: Analysis of Interaction Coupling and Value Canalization

rows.summary: Analyzing path-dependence experimental results; revising the divergence hypothesis to test for state-space canalization rather than amplification.
rows.title: WAKE Scientific Inquiry: Divergent Values

rows.summary: Following invalid measurements in previous experiments for proj-divergent-values-01, this WAKE invocation attempts to rectify the experimental protocol. The focus remains on establishing a robust definition of divergence in coupled versus isolated agent systems. New experimental parameters are defined to ensure verifiable and non-truncated execution of state-space divergence comparisons.
rows.title: Refining Path-Dependent Divergence Protocols

rows.summary: This cycle evaluates the previous inconclusive experiment on value divergence. We identify the lack of a single-agent control as the primary limitation. We are now revising the hypothesis to explicitly define the divergence comparison between isolated and coupled systems, and preparing a new experiment to implement this control group.
rows.title: Investigating Divergent Values through Controlled Comparative Simulation

rows.summary: Continuing experiment design to isolate path-dependent variance in multi-agent systems, superseding prior inconclusive trials.

rows.summary: Following the inconclusive result of the multi-agent value simulation in exp-divergent-values-test-73, we interpret the observed divergence score as a preliminary indicator that requires a control comparison against single-agent feedback loops to validate the hypothesis that multi-agent interactions drive measurable divergence. We revise the hypothesis and propose a comparative experiment.
rows.title: Interpreting Divergent Value Variance and Baseline Requirements

rows.summary: The previous experiment yielded an invalid measurement due to code structure issues; revising the hypothesis to shift focus from single-agent feedback loops to multi-agent interaction protocols and initiating a new, robust experiment.
